files.README.md:
# Fernweh & Co.

A small sample web shop selling travel gear: backpacks, water bottles and
trail maps. This project exists to give the demo workspace something real to
work on: a handful of pages, a tiny Flask app, and a month of sample sales.

## Layout

- `src/app.py`: the shop's tiny storefront, a few routes, no database.
- `docs/notes.md`: running notes from the last content review.
- `data/sales.csv`: one month of sample orders, by category.

Nothing here talks to a real payment provider or a real warehouse. It is a
sandbox for the demo agents: the Demo Writer edits the copy, the Demo Analyst
reads the sales data, and the Demo Reviewer signs off before anything counts
as done.
files.docs/notes.md:
# Content review notes

Running notes from the last pass over the storefront copy. Kept short on
purpose: this is a demo project, not a real backlog.

## Open items

- The catalog page still reads a little flat. A one-line description per
  product would help more than another adjective on the headline.
- "About" is one sentence. That is probably fine for a shop this size, but it
  could name what makes the gear different (weight, materials) rather than
  just tone.
- No pricing copy explains why the Trailpack costs more than the bottle. A
  short note on materials would answer the obvious question.

## Done

- Renamed "Rucksack 32" to "Trailpack 32L" everywhere, including the sales
  data, so the name is consistent end to end.
- Confirmed the three product categories (Backpacks, Bottles, Maps) match
  what is actually sold in `data/sales.csv`.

## What the numbers show

Backpacks bring in the most revenue this month even though Bottles sell in
higher volume: the Trailpack's higher price makes up for fewer units. Maps are
the smallest line but the steadiest seller day to day.

spec.title: Fernweh & Co.: August content report
spec.markdown:
# August content report

## Content

The catalog, product and about pages were reviewed this month. The Trailpack
32L was renamed from "Rucksack 32" everywhere, including the sample sales
data, so the name is consistent end to end.

## Sales

Backpacks were the top revenue category in August ($1,780), ahead of Bottles
($1,200) and Maps ($645), even though Bottles sold in higher volume. See the
attached chart and table for the day-by-day breakdown.

## Next

Add a one-line description per product on the catalog page, and a short note
on materials to explain the Trailpack's price.

```python

    {"slug": "trailpack-32", "name": "Trailpack 32L", "price": 89.00, "category": "Backpacks"},
    {"slug": "summit-bottle", "name": "Summit Bottle 1L", "price": 24.00, "category": "Bottles"},
    {"slug": "ridge-map-pack", "name": "Ridge Map Pack", "price": 15.00, "category": "Maps"},
]
```

Backpacks bring in the most revenue this month even though Bottles sell in higher volume, since the Trailpack costs more per unit.
